description: Read an offered location unchanged: {"location": "the offered location"}. The host supplies the content and its reusable identity; do not construct a new selection name from a source name. Omit select for the default read; use an explicit selector only for a particular part. Returns actual content and pinned locations. Omitted selection reads bounded content (images: overview); large records return a directory. Source, derived and model work remain distinct. Use only selectors supported by that location. Reading never saves conclusions. select is one flat object with a required kind, not a string or a nested kind wrapper. Read several things at once with items; reading one thing may name its location and select directly instead. What you can still see is not sent twice: reading it again answers IN_CONTEXT and is not progress. Earlier reads that have left your context are listed under earlier_reads with how to read them again. select example: {"kind":"text_range","start_sentence":0,"end_sentence":2}. select example: {"kind":"text_part","part":0}. select example: {"kind":"image_region","frame":"source","region":{"left":500,"top":0,"right":1000,"bottom":400}}. select example: {"kind":"record_items","fields":["text"]}. select example: {"kind":"directory","offset":0,"limit":5}. select example: {"kind":"whole"}. select example: {"kind":"query","terms":"convergent fragment coupling"}.

oneOf.description: Request the complete bounded resource; exceeding the budget is an error.

Take sentences by position when the whole text is more than the question needs.

Sentences are numbered by the handler's own segmentation, starting at 0, and end is
exclusive. A read that returned a directory has already named the ranges it offers.

Copy a host-offered part of oversized saved text, without computing offsets.

Parts are transport slices of the pinned record, not source sentences or new
evidence. Only locations that offer these entries support this selector.

part.description: Copy the part number from the offered read entry.

oneOf.description: Select original-image coordinates, normalized to 1000; return exact pixels.

frame.description: Use this location’s authorized original image, including for saved crops.

region.description: Named original-image edges normalized to 1000; origin top-left. left/right increase rightwards; top/bottom increase downwards.

oneOf.description: Read offered entries/fields or a JSON Pointer within the pinned resource.
Read a bounded page of child locations, not the children's full contents.

Find authorized text by what it says, when its location is not known yet.

In source investigations, TERMS containing only a known authorized source name,
location or canonical page name returns its read entries as named_sources, not
text matches or read evidence. A canonical package address not in the authorized
catalog returns no navigation match; it is not split into content words.
LITERAL always searches the words in source text.
TERMS returns FULL blocks covering all query words when any exist; it does not fill remaining slots with weaker matches. Otherwise it returns only the best available PARTIAL coverage, with matched_terms naming the words actually found; a lone single-character fragment cannot support a partial multiword query. A standalone word, element or number remains searchable. Explicit superscripts on lexical words also permit finding their base word, while preserving the original full spelling; ordinary trailing digits are not removed. Double-quoted phrases must match a continuous string. LITERAL matches the normalized continuous query including symbols. Neither mode expands stems, prefixes, wildcards or scientific synonyms. 
There are no operators, so OR and AND are ordinary words. A hit names a location and the
sentences that matched in it, numbered as text_range counts them: sentence is the
start; end_sentence, when present, is exclusive and covers a cross-sentence match.
Read the location with that range, or a range around a single sentence for
its context, or without select for the whole block. Long snippets marked search_preview
use the index's rendered text around the match; read the source before quoting it.
A hit whose matching range is covered by a known valid read says so
(read: turns_ago, and whether it is still shown); no hint means coverage is unproven,
and the location remains readable. A search that found exactly what
an earlier one found says so (same_hits_as) and is not progress. Finding nothing
means nothing matched *this* query within the authorized scope; it is never evidence
that a concept is absent from the paper.
